text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: Multiple customer reports of spikes in 5xxs + large latency from EU -> US regions. Auto-routing errors observed. Investigating. thread id 2034567890

jake_oncall: i'm on it. seeing a ~30% increase in 502/504 from eu-west->us-west over last 3m. also some DNS NXDOMAIN flaps in the edge logs. pulling routing policy audit now.

maria_netops: looking. last routing policy deploy was region-fallback-v2 (rollout 2026-03-15T01:02Z). i see a rule that falls through to nearest region when pin missing. could be matching broad prefix.

oliver_prod: any customer visible impact numbers? tara_support, have you got tickets?

tara_support: yes — 6 high-impact CS tickets since 01:05Z, mostly error responses and timeouts for customers pinned to eu-west. customers report requests landing in us-west and timing out. i've looped in account teams.

jake_oncall: grabbing example request traces. here's a diagnostic query i ran from the edge:```bash
# diagnostics from edge 10.4.2.11
curl -v -H "X-Region-Pref: eu-west" "https://edge.redwood.ai/ping?trace=2034567890"
* Connected to edge.redwood.ai (10.4.2.11) port 443 \n> GET /ping?trace=2034567890 HTTP/1.1
> Host: edge.redwood.ai
> X-Region-Pref: eu-west
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< x-route-policy: region-fallback-v2
< x-proxied-to: us-west-2a
```
this shows the policy is selecting us-west even when header requests eu-west.

maria_netops: confirming. policy rules are matching by ASG tag first, then prefix fallback. a recent regex change widened the prefix matcher and dropped an explicit "pin" check. looks like a logic regression in the rollout.

ryan_enginfra: i can push a quick temporary gate in the edge routing: deny the fallthrough behavior for requests with X-Region-Pref header. small config change, no model code. i have the patch ready.

oliver_prod: recommended next steps? rollback? patch? customer comms?

jake_oncall: immediate plan: 1) apply edge gate to honor X-Region-Pref (mitigation) 2) rollback region-fallback-v2 to region-fallback-v1 in routing configs if gate not cleanly working 3) open severity notice and coord CS comms. tagging @maria_netops to validate rollback safety.

maria_netops: agree. gate first — lower blast radius. if gate clears 5m of synthetic checks, then we can decide on rollback. I'll stand by to validate.

pagerduty-bot: jake_oncall acknowledged the page at 2034567905 (P0).

ryan_enginfra: deploying gate now to edge pool eu-west-edge-01..03 (rolling). command:```sh
infractl route-config apply --edge eu-west-edge --set honor_region_pref=true --reason "hotfix: mitigate region fallthrough"
```
estimated 60s per host, will stream progress.

(2m later)

ryan_enginfra: :eyes: gate applied to eu-west-edge-01/02. eu-west-edge-03 in progress.

jake_oncall: running synthetic vs customer-visible errors:```
# quick synthetic
curl -s -H "X-Region-Pref: eu-west" https://edge.redwood.ai/ping | jq -r .region
# before: us-west-2a, after gate: eu-west-1b
```
results: pre-gate snapshots show ~70% misroutes to us-west, post-gate samples show 98% honoring eu-west. 5xx rate dropped from 30%->4% in eu-west path.

tara_support: cs notified customers in the impacted cohort with a short note: "we're mitigating a routing issue causing requests to route out of your region; mitigation in progress; next update in 30m."

oliver_prod: good. do we have a rollback plan if gate fails? maria?

maria_netops: rollback plan: revert to region-fallback-v1 (commit a8f3e1) via config manager. rollback window is 10m. rollback command:```sh
infractl route-config promote --policy region-fallback-v1 --env prod --reason "emergency rollback" --dry-run=false
```
we won't rollback yet unless gate shows instability.

(another 4m)

jake_oncall: gate looks stable for 6m. 5xxs reduced, latency back within SLOs for impacted customers. i'm going to mark the incident as mitigated and start the handoff to next oncall for monitoring.

pagerduty-bot: escalation timeout updated; next monitor checkpoint in 30m.

ryan_enginfra: pushed a short-term config hotfix to ensure the explicit pin check is evaluated before broad prefix matching. this is a conservative change and will be part of a follow-up revert to the rollout. change id: hotfix/2034567890-pin-check.

jake_oncall: handoff notes for night oncall: incident 2034567890 — root cause: routing policy regression in region-fallback-v2 that dropped explicit pin check, causing fallthrough to nearest region. mitigation: gate honor_region_pref=true applied to eu-west edges and small hotfix to re-evaluate pin checks. customer impact: several customers experienced timeouts and 5xx when requests were misrouted to US region; CS engaged and tickets opened. ongoing: monitor for 60m, prepare full rollback if any relapse. links: infra change https://internal.redwood/changes/hotfix/2034567890, ticket 20421.

tara_support: adding CS summary to ticket 20421 and sending a follow-up to impacted accounts once stable :white_check_mark:.

oliver_prod: can we tag this for a postmortem? i'd like a timeline + diff of the routing policy rollout and a review of our canary heuristics.

jake_oncall: yes — creating postmortem stub now and assigning action items: - policy deploy checklist to include explicit pin unit tests - improve canary traffic shape to include pinned-header cases - add synthetic: test honoring X-Region-Pref across edges.

maria_netops: will also audit recent policy changes for similar regressions and add a short-term rollback guard to the deploy pipeline.

(incident-bot): INCIDENT MITIGATED :white_check_mark: — mitigation applied at 2034568020. please continue monitoring and file postmortem.

jake_oncall: handing off to night shift @ryan_enginfra for observation. i'll keep the incident ticket warm for final runbook notes.

ryan_enginfra: taking over monitoring. ping me if any regression.

(End of thread)
